introduction: Today the Church celebrates the Annunciation of the Lord. It falls on 25 March, nine months before Christmas; when that day comes in Holy Week or the Easter Octave, the solemnity is moved to the Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter. The angel Gabriel brings God's message to Mary, and she answers yes. The Son of God takes flesh in her womb. During the Creed, at the words about the Incarnation, we kneel. Let us adore the Word made flesh and learn from Mary's yes.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Word became flesh and lived among us. With Mary, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Mary, she may listen to God's word and say yes to his plan for the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For expectant mothers and for unborn children: that every human life may be welcomed and protected from its very beginning. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are discerning their vocation: that they may hear God's call and answer it with generosity and trust. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who face an unexpected change in their lives: that they may find peace in knowing that nothing is impossible with God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make Mary's words our own each day: let it be done to me according to your word. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, at the message of an angel your Son took flesh in the womb of the Virgin Mary. Help us to welcome your will as she did, and to bring Christ to the world. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Let it be done to me
reflection.body:
Nine months before Christmas, the Church celebrates the moment when the Son of God became man. It is a feast of the Lord and a feast of Mary at the same time.

Centuries before, Isaiah gave a sign to a king who would not ask for one: "Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." Immanuel means God with us.

In Nazareth, an ordinary town in Galilee, the angel Gabriel greets a young woman: "Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you." Mary is troubled, and Gabriel reassures her: "Don't be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God." He tells her she will bear a son who will be called "the Son of the Most High."

Mary does not doubt God; she asks how it will happen. The answer is the Holy Spirit: "The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you." And Gabriel adds the sentence that holds the whole feast: "For nothing spoken by God is impossible."

Then Mary gives her answer: "Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word." The Letter to the Hebrews hears the same yes in the Son himself: "Behold, I have come to do your will." At the Annunciation, the yes of Mary and the yes of the Son meet, and God takes flesh.

This is why we kneel during the Creed today, at the words about the Incarnation. God came close enough to be carried in a womb. This week, pray the Angelus or a Hail Mary slowly, and offer God your own yes in whatever he is asking of you now.
